text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #7448d1

g.text: IN PLAIN ENGLISH
For the critical path, add execution times along each required chain
and take the longest. For slack, subtract all estimated remaining work
and waits from the time left before the deadline.
rho: one dependency path; CP: longest required work chain, excluding queue waits.
sigma: estimated spare time; W_hat_rem: remaining-time estimate, including waits.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #7448d1

g.text: WORKED RAP EXAMPLE
Drum path: 100 + 50 = 150 ms.
Later: now t = 6,000 ms; deadline D = 7,800 ms.
Estimate remaining work and waits as 1,500 ms.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #7448d1

g.text: Estimated spare time: 300 ms
An extra 600-ms wait changes slack to -300 ms.
This is a hypothetical estimate, not a fitted predictor.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #7448d1

g.text: WHAT THIS TELLS US
Parallel work should not be counted as if every stage ran in sequence. The critical path is a lower bound
on required execution time; using it alone as a completion forecast ignores waiting and input availability.
